G-00001.statement: Thyroid disorders, particularly hypothyroidism, are frequently reported as comorbidities among people with lipedema.

G-00002.statement: Thyroid disease or hypothyroidism is reported more often in lipedema than in general-population or clinical comparison groups in unadjusted cross-sectional comparisons.

G-00003.statement: After multivariable adjustment for other factors, hypothyroidism may not be independently associated with lipedema.

G-00004.statement: In women with painful lipedema, liposuction reduces leg pain more than conservative therapy alone.

G-00005.statement: Liposuction for lipedema is associated with reductions in pain, edema, bruising, heaviness and other symptoms compared with preoperative status.

G-00006.statement: Liposuction for lipedema is associated with improved quality of life and mobility.

G-00007.statement: Liposuction for lipedema may be associated with improved psychological wellbeing and body image.

G-00008.statement: Improvements after liposuction for lipedema are reported to persist for years without clinically relevant deterioration.

G-00009.statement: Liposuction for lipedema is associated with reduced need for compression and other conservative decongestive therapy.

G-00010.statement: Major complications after liposuction for lipedema are uncommon, while minor complications such as seroma and hematoma occur more often.

G-00011.statement: Benefits of liposuction for lipedema may be more sustained in earlier than in advanced disease stages.

G-00012.statement: Much non-randomised evidence on liposuction for lipedema consists of uncontrolled before-after studies with substantial risk of bias.
